pages.title: What this unit is about
pages.body:
> 🧩 **Strand 4 — Computational Thinking**
Sub-strand 3: Robotics

Every robot, from a toy to a factory arm, has a brain, a body and senses. In this unit you will learn how the controller, the mechanical parts and the sensors work together, and where sensors are used in everyday life.

pages.title: Content standard and lessons
pages.body:

**Core competencies developed:** Communication and Collaboration (CC8.2), Critical Thinking (CP5.2).

pages.title: Controller, Actuators and Sensors
pages.body:
Curriculum indicator B8.4.3.1.1
> 🎯 **Learning objectives** By the end of this lesson you should be able to:
- explain the controller as the brain of the robot;
- describe mechanical parts (actuators);
- describe how sensors input data and their real-life uses.
[[fig:c8-f20|Figure 19: How the parts of a robot work together]]
## The controller: the “brain”
The **controller** is a computer (often a small **microcontroller** such as an Arduino, or a single-board computer such as a Raspberry Pi or micro:bit) that runs the robot’s **program**. It receives data from the sensors, decides what to do, and sends commands to the actuators. Without a program, the controller does nothing.
## Mechanical parts: actuators
| **Part** | **What it does** |
|---|---|
| Motors (DC motors, servo motors, stepper motors) | Convert electrical energy into movement; servos turn to a precise angle |
| Wheels and tracks | Let the robot move around |
| Gears | Change speed and force (torque) of movement |
| Pistons (hydraulic/pneumatic) | Push and lift heavy loads with liquid or air pressure |
| Grippers / end effectors | Grab, hold and release objects like a hand |
| Joints and arms | Allow turning, bending and lifting |
## Sensors: the robot’s senses
**Sensors** measure physical properties of the robot’s surroundings and condition and send the readings to the controller as **input data**. Sensors are also used in many computer-controlled systems that are not robots.

pages.title: Controller, Actuators and Sensors (continued)
pages.body:
| **Sensor** | **Measures** | **Real-life uses** |
|---|---|---|
| Light | Brightness | Street lights that switch on at dusk; automatic phone screen brightness; line-following robots |
| Temperature | Heat | Air conditioners and fridges (thermostats); incubators; fire alarms; car engines |
| Magnetic field | Magnets / metal | Door and window security alarms; phone compass; vehicle detection at traffic lights |
| Gas | Gases in the air | Smoke and carbon monoxide detectors; LPG leak alarms in kitchens; pollution monitoring |
| Pressure | Force or pressure | Weighing scales; tyre pressure; touchscreens; burglar alarm pressure mats |
| Moisture | Water content | Automatic irrigation of farms when soil is dry |
| Humidity | Water vapour in air | Weather stations; greenhouses; museums; egg incubators |
| pH | Acidity / alkalinity | Water quality testing; swimming pools; fish farming; soil testing |
| Motion (PIR, ultrasonic, infrared) | Movement / distance | Security lights; automatic doors; obstacle-avoiding robots; game controllers; parking sensors |
> ✏️ **Worked example — A street light control system**
1. The **light sensor** measures brightness every minute.
2. The controller’s program checks: IF light level < dusk value THEN switch lamp ON, ELSE switch lamp OFF.
3. The **actuator** (a relay switch) turns the lamp on or off.
4. The loop repeats all night: this is **feedback control**.

pages.title: Controller, Actuators and Sensors (continued)
pages.body:
> 🧪 **Activity**
Watch a video or study pictures of the parts of a robot (e.g. a robotic arm, a line-following robot or a robot vacuum). Label the controller, sensors and actuators, and explain how they work together.

pages.title: Review: written and practical tasks
pages.body:
> ✏️ **Review exercises** — answer these in your exercise book or on the computer, then check with your teacher.
## Short answer questions
1. Explain the functions of the controller, actuators and sensors of a robot.
2. Name **five** sensors and give one real-life use of each.
3. Describe how a security light uses a motion sensor.
